_comment: Same node-pairing flow as a bare ESP32 button, but this device gets its OWN dedicated agent (this preset) instead of binding to an existing one, since it needs the stackchan MCP tools nothing else has.
steps: 1. Pair the physical unit - same steps as scripts/agent-presets/esp32-node/trigger.json.
2. Deploy this preset with a unique __AGENT_ID__ per physical unit (e.g. stackchan-bret, stackchan-family).
3. Start the stackchan-mcp bridge server for that unit (see docs/stackchan-mcp-and-memory-2026-09-03.md - needs its own .env with that robot's IP, host IP, Fish Audio key).
4. Bind that node to this agent, same pattern as esp32-node/trigger.json's bind_to_existing_agent, pointed at THIS agent's id instead.
open_question: Not yet verified: exact tool names the stackchan-mcp bridge actually exposes. Confirm with the bridge's own docs or `openclaw mcp list-tools` once connected, before trusting the mcp:stackchan_* allow pattern in agent-template.json.
